findings.issue: A hand-rolled TTL/LRU promise cache plus a FIFO concurrency limiter reimplements data caching that the framework already provides (fetch with next:{revalidate:60}, or 'use cache' under cacheComponents); ~60 lines of infra the team must own, test and explain.
findings.suggestion: Use the framework's fetch caching (or 'use cache' when adopting cacheComponents) and drop the custom cache; keep withSlot only if the local API genuinely needs a concurrency cap, with a comment saying why.

findings.issue: The concurrency limiter can overshoot MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS: a released slot can be grabbed by a newly arriving request before a queued waiter's resolve runs, and waiters don't re-check the cap on wake.
findings.suggestion: Re-check active >= MAX after the await, or document that the cap is best-effort.

findings.issue: 404 responses are cached as null for the full 60-second TTL, so a resource that appears on the API stays 'Not found' for up to a minute.
findings.suggestion: Use a much shorter (or zero) negative TTL for null results, or a comment noting the trade-off is intentional.

findings.issue: Default-variety → default-Pokémon resolution is duplicated verbatim in app/src/app/team/page.tsx:35-36.
findings.suggestion: Extract a getDefaultPokemon(species) helper next to getSpecies in lib/api.ts.

findings.issue: Query-string building is duplicated between pageHref (page.tsx:20) and href (filters.tsx:11); they must stay in sync (defaults omitted, page reset).
findings.suggestion: Share one buildQuery(filters, page?) helper in lib.

findings.issue: No error.tsx or loading.tsx anywhere: an API failure throws inside page render and produces the default framework 500, and data-heavy pages block with no streamed shell or pending state.
findings.suggestion: Add a root error.tsx with a friendly message and a loading.tsx (or Suspense boundaries) around the heavy data loads.

findings.issue: getSpeciesIndex() already fetches all types and generations internally; the page fetches both again for the dropdowns, and the 1025-entry index is rebuilt on every request (only the underlying fetches are cached).
findings.suggestion: Have getSpeciesIndex return the types/generations it loaded, and consider memoising the assembled index for the cache TTL.

findings.issue: spriteUrl hardcodes the API's media path pattern (/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png) with no comment; it's sanctioned by SPEC.md but embeds unexplained API knowledge.
findings.suggestion: Add a comment citing the documented sprite pattern, or fall back to the API-provided front_default URL when available.

findings.issue: eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element comment, but the project has no ESLint config or dependency — the directive is dead weight.
findings.suggestion: Either add eslint + eslint-config-next to the devDependencies, or drop the disable comments.

findings.issue: Team mutation writes document.cookie directly from the client; the framework's supported path for cookie writes is a Server Action (or route handler) using cookies().set().
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as a deliberate, simple choice (avoids a round trip before refresh), but consider a Server Action for consistency; if kept, note why in a comment.

summary: A disciplined, current-generation App Router implementation — async params, cache-deduped loaders, notFound(), connection()-driven request-time rendering, and a cookie-based feature that renders server-side so state never flashes. The one structural reservation is the bespoke fetch cache/concurrency layer where the framework already provides caching, plus a couple of duplicated helpers and missing error/loading boundaries. I'd merge after one comment round.
